reply_text:
㊥ Gist: For 22 August to today, 21 turns are left: 16 still being read and 5 that the checker refused. Older periods have much more missing. July has 1,281 turns waiting to be read, and most of 1–21 August and everything from February to June has never been split into batches at all.

㊢ (target window, from `xiang_coverage.py` just now) 4,915 of 4,936 read (99.6%).
- **The 22 August–21 September window** and the **22–26 September batch** are now fully read.
- **The eight 26–27 September turns:** 6 read and 2 refused by the checker.
- **Live turns:** 16 pending and 3 refused. Of the 16:
  - 10 are retry-block turns from 30 September that the loop hasn't published yet; they may be in a pack still running;
  - 6 are from today, waiting for the usual live reader.
  - Once a turn has failed twice, the loop gives up on it.

㊢ (older periods)

| period | state |
|---|---|
| July | 2,067 batched, 758 read, 28 refused, **1,281 pending**. The loop has started on these. |
| 1–21 August | only one block of 100 was ever built (93 read). The rest of those three weeks has no batch yet. |
| February–June | about 5,000 turns, almost none read (`E-象-catchup.md`). No batches built. |

The two unbuilt periods need `turn_batch.py build` runs, and those should apply today's harness filter, since that period predates origin stamping.

㊟ (pace) Since the restart at 20:34, the four seats have published 58 turns in about 16 minutes, roughly 200 an hour. At that rate July would take 6–7 hours. The loop is set to stop at 00:34 UTC, so it will get partway through.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Almost. Fetching the data for 21 September to today is now low-risk, because the extraction script already takes `--since` and `--before`. The fetch is the smaller part of the job, though. The main work is hand-reading every pattern retrieved since 21 September that isn't among the 689 already labelled. I'd do it in two steps: run the fetch and count the unlabelled patterns, then label them in packs. Shall I send step one to a Kimi or Zai seat?

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (on "without alarm bells") Today I measured single pages, at 0.07–0.40 s each. I have no record of how futon1b behaved during the 6m24s run on 21 September; the method note says only that it paged with `limit=1000` and made no deep health query. It's probably fine, but I haven't checked it. Step one will record futon1b's heap and query slots before and after the fetch, so we'll know.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the extension needs besides the fetch)
- **New patterns to label:** each turn's stage comes from a hand label on the pattern it retrieved. On the 21 September re-run, 94 newly retrieved patterns had to be read by hand. Ten days of new work, covering 象, the Morning Brief and the War Machine contract, will add more. I don't know how many until the fetch has run.
- **Your-turn count:** before 27 September, park wake-ups were filed as your turns. The Minard filter removes resume markers by their text, but it predates some wake formats. Step one should also run `xiang2000_p6o3.classify`, the filter I used today, and report any turns where the two filters disagree.
- **Token panel:** the figure's lower panel comes from a separate report of Codex token use in the gaps between your turns. That report would need regenerating to cover the new dates. Without it, the figure for the new dates has only its upper panel.
- **Hard-coded dates:** `minard_operator_work.py` has its start and end dates written in. That's a small edit.
